newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French interest rate futures were boosted by a 10 basis point cut in the intervention rate which helped bond futures outperform Bund futures while a stronger franc provided a favourable backdrop.

Widespread expectations for a post-budget intervention rate cut were dampened slightly this morning when call money was left unchanged, allowing the December PIBOR to gain ground over the equivalent Euromark contract when rates were eventually cut.
Traders said the rate cut also spurred interest in the the two-year area of the curve, following solid demand from primary dealers at the Treasury auction earlier in the day.

Economists were as divided on the likelihood of an interest rate cut, forecasts had ranged from a 20 basis point reduction to no change, as they were on the scope for further cuts without another move from Germany.

While all saw the cut in the rate to 3.25 percent as an apparant sign of the Bank of France's approval of the 1997 budget unveiled on Wednesday, some said it had further room to narrow the 25 basis point spread over the German repo rate.
"By only catching up with the Bundesbank they've signalled they're being cautious. They could have done more and been OK," Sonja Gibbs, bond strategist at Nomura International, said.
The French central bank only trimmed the French intervention rate by 20 basis points on August 22 when the Bundesbank cut its repo rate by 30 basis points.
One trader at a French bank said demand for two-year bonds was helped by the cut with one non-resident in particular buying a large amount of 1998 BTANs.
Earlier, the Treasury sold 9.38 billion francs of October 1998 BTANs with a cover of 3.4 and 8.485 billion of October 2001 BTANs with a cover of 2.7.
Ciaran O'Hagan, bond analyst at JP Morgan in Paris, said he was surprised the two-year area had remained so well supported.
"It's very surprising it's held in so well despite a budget which didn't show structural reform, mark/Paris weakness and only 10 basis points off the intervention rate," said O'Hagan.

Nevertheless, he said there was scope for the two-year spread over German bonds to narrow to 40 basis points by the end of October from 48 now. He said French two-year bonds looked cheap given how flat the two-to-five year area of the curve was compared with the five-to-10 year area.
The spread between December PIBOR and December Euromarks narrowed to 58 basis points after the BoF rate cut, close to the lowest for the year.

Traders said the bond future remained stuck in a fairly narrow range on Thursday and that it would probably remain that way ahead of the Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee meeting on September 24.
"We had buyers on the dips and good selling at the highs, this market is massively range bound," said a Matif trader at a French bank.
For most of the session the contract traded between 123.80 and 124.00, hitting its high of 124.02 soon after the Bank of France rate cut, boosted by non-resident buying of the contract, traders said.

There was continued speculation about when welfare debt repayment fund CADES would return to the bond market. Several syndication managers said there was a chance it could issue more French franc bonds as early as next week.

One said he expected another 15-18 billion of the 2002 and 2007 bonds CADES has already sold. Another said the 2002 bond was trading well and that CADES might issue it as well as a new maturity. He said the size could be anywhere from 10 to 20 billion francs.
"There's no auction next week and it's the best opportunity for several weeks, so it's not too far-fetched."
